name: Question 11
problem:
A particle $P$ of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is subject to the external forces 

$$
{F}_{1}=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,8t⟩,\,{F}_{2}=⟨4,\,0⟩,
$$

where ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}$ are measured in newtons and $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the velocity of $P$ equals $⟨0,\,1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at $t=2\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

$v(2)=$
$⟨\,$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$\,⟩\,m/s$
worked_solution:
Newton's second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

The resultant force $F$ acting on $P$ equals the sum of the forces acting on $P.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F & ={F}_{1}+{F}_{2} \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,8t⟩+⟨4,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4,\,8t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

By Newton's second law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{F}{m} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4,\,8t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1,\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the velocity vector $v,$ we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\int a\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1,\,2t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t,\,\int (2t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a (vector) constant of integration. 

We can solve for $C$ by substituting $v=⟨0,\,1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ and $t=0\,\text{s}$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨0,\,1⟩ & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡0+0,\,{0}^{2}⟩+C \\ ⟨0,\,1⟩ & =⟨0,\,0⟩+C \\ C & =⟨0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t,\,{t}^{2}⟩+⟨0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t,\,{t}^{2}+1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity at $t=2$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2)+2,\,{2}^{2}+1⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2)+2,\,5⟩\,m/s.\end{aligned}
$$
